## TL;DR

Review round 1 exposed that the original verification covered only the Detected tab, while the reported screenshot came from the default-agents model notice. I reproduced that notice path with a fake Cursor CLI returning the reported bare `agent login` guidance and a credential-shaped sentinel. Cursor model-probe authentication errors now use a canonical `cursor-agent login` instruction and discard raw stderr. Tests cover the CLI failure, the rendered default-agent notice, and both Detected-tab states.

## Work and rationale

The screenshot corresponds to a model-list probe, not the Detected tab. `src/core/models.ts` previously forwarded the first non-empty Cursor stderr line into the model result. The config store then included that raw reason in the default-agents notice. Cursor CLI auth failure output can tell users to run a bare `agent login`, which is inconsistent with the binary RepoOS actually detects and launches (`cursor-agent`) and can collide with other tools on PATH.

I added `src/core/cursor-auth.ts` as the shared source for the canonical login command and a narrow auth-error classifier. The Cursor model adapter uses it to replace recognizable authentication stderr with fixed guidance: run `cursor-agent login` and retry. The raw error is not attached to this auth result, so vendor stderr and credential-shaped text cannot pass through this path. The detected-agent auth hint and remote-runner setup command now use the same login-command constant. Run-time Cursor failure guidance also uses the constant, keeping the primary remediation consistent across model loading, detection, runner setup, and agent turns.

The model adapter regression test runs a fake `cursor-agent --list-models` that exits with stderr containing the bare `agent login` suggestion and a fake `CURSOR_API_KEY` value. It asserts that the result uses the canonical guidance and excludes the sentinel. The Agents component test mounts the default tab, supplies that sanitized failed model result, and verifies the visible model notice includes the user action. The detected-tab component test now asserts the actual status pill and hint-code presence/absence: authenticated means ready with no auth hint; unauthenticated means sign-in required with the canonical login command and a copy action.

## Approaches tried

I traced the model adapter through the config store to the default-agent notice and compared its behavior with the detected-agent probe and run-time error mapper. A test fixture reproduces the CLI-auth failure without requiring a real Cursor account or touching local credentials. The classifier is intentionally scoped to recognizable auth failures; ordinary model-list errors retain their existing diagnostics. I chose fixed text for auth failures because forwarding the vendor line is both inconsistent and unnecessary for remediation.

## Challenges and blockers

No live Cursor credential was available, so external Cursor service authentication was not claimed. The behavior under review is a local CLI response-to-UI path and is deterministically covered with the fake binary. The fake credential-shaped value exists only in test stderr; it is asserted absent from the returned error. No user action is required to verify the product behavior.

## Key learnings

The default Agents page reports the model-list probe's failure separately from the Detected tab's CLI auth status and from RepoOS account authentication. Those are distinct surfaces but should point to the same executable-specific sign-in action. A model probe should not render raw authentication stderr when it can contain credential-shaped material. A shared command constant prevents the detected-agent hint, model notice, and remote-runner command from drifting back to a bare `agent` invocation.
